title: Prescription drug info key to inquiry
article: Tuesday's continuation of the fatality inquiry of 25-year-old Colleen Marie Akazay - found dead in her cell the morning of Feb. 18, 2006 - focused largely on events from the hours leading to her death.
When it was last in session in November 2007, the focus was more on medical and prescription history and how it may have contributed.
Prescription records revealed Akazay had been prescribed 180 tablets of the sedative bromazepam - a supply typically meant to last four to six months - six weeks before her death.
She had also been prescribed 100 tablets of Tylenol 4 less than 72 hours before her death.

She was said by her physician, Dr. Andries Botha, to have had a variety of health problems, ranging from chronic back pain to depression, anxiety and stress disorders. Akazay had prescriptions from Botha for all of these.
Prescription records show she had also been "triple-doctoring," meaning two other doctors besides Botha were giving her access to medication.
Akazay was also said to have been buying non-prescription, extra-strength Tylenol pills by the hundreds.
Evidence was found she had used cocaine prior to her death, though that was not considered a contributing factor.
Traces of methadone - a painkiller often used to aid in heroin and morphine withdrawal - were also found in her system. This may have made a minor contribution.
All of this was considered to be in excess of what could be called "average therapeutic dosage," and Botha said he would have reconsidered his prescriptions had he known of her activities.
Most of the multiple bottles found on Akazay were only missing pills in an amount consistent with prescribed usage, but a 20-tablet bottle of Tylenol 3 had only two tablets left.

Only 10 to 12 of those 18 missing tablets would be needed to cause a codeine concentration as high as was found in her blood - nearly twice as high as what would be considered lethal, according to Alberta's chief toxicologist Graham Jones.
Jones said five or six of the Tylenol 4 tablets in her possession also would have done it.
